classification.difficultyReason: Count the two requested colour categories among equal sectors, then apply f = np.

content.prompt:
Consider the spinner.
How many times would you expect it to land on green or red in 200 spins?

spec.description: Ten equal sectors, clockwise from the top boundary: G, R, B, G, R, B, G, R, B, B. Black boundaries, central pivot and upward pointer. Labelled multicolour sectors require TikZ rather than the fraction-circle template.
spec.mathematics: Three green, three red and four blue equal sectors; six of ten sectors are green or red.
spec.answerVisibility: Spinner and all labels remain visible in the question; no calculated probability or expected frequency is supplied.

answer.worked:
There are 3 green and 3 red sectors out of 10 equal sectors.
$P(\text{green or red})=\frac{3+3}{10}=\frac{3}{5}$.
$$\begin{align*}f&=np\\&=200\times\frac{3}{5}\\&=120\text{ times}\end{align*}$$
